    - Sitting. I am sitting. Look at me, sitting, with my foot on a cushion like a grandee. Has the message gone to Perch yet? Do not answer. Just go.

    - There is my test runner! I have run the tower line three more times since you. It still breaks at the Long Lean. One day it will not.

    - Gate Walk to the Great Hall, by the roofs. A sand-glass at each end, turned by somebody honest. I took the record last summer and bettered it twice since.
    - Cobble keeps the times on the back of his shop door. Tick means to beat it by the streets, and writes down everybody who says he cannot. I have not said it. I am waiting to say it at the finish.
    - My grandmother ran messages over these roofs when Cobble was young. She taught me the old routes: the long jump over the Night Market, the gutter run below the Crooked Tower, the singing slates.
    - My mother ran too, until a wet roof took her knee. She lives out near Kaldemor now and writes when the carts get through. Three of us in Cobble's boots. I am the fastest. Do not tell my mother.
    - Ask Nana Gristle on her bench in Lantern Square. She has a list as long as your arm. Half of them fell in fifty years ago and were patched. The other half... well. Ask Nana. Do not tell her I sent you.
    - Do not say it so loud. The roof over the old cooper's yard. She said it would go, and it went, and I was on it. Fine. She was right. Once.
